name: NSRegularExpression (vs Swift Regex)
baseline: Swift Regex (Regex literals and Regex(String), Swift 5.7 to 6.3)
verdict_reason: NSRegularExpression is much cheaper to construct (0.036 s vs 0.677 s for 10,000 patterns) and avoids some of Swift Regex's backtracking blow-ups (4x faster in a Swift 6.1.2 report). But with the Regex hoisted to a static, a real linting workload ran within 0.7% of NSRegularExpression. The advantage is mostly construction and pathological patterns, not everyday matching.
tier_reason: Independent user measurements in Swift Forums, swift-format and swift-experimental-string-processing issues, with toolchains and some hardware stated; no single controlled suite.
claimed_speedup: Construction, 10000 times: Swift Regex 0.677 s vs NSRegularExpression 0.036 s (18.8x, derived from page data). Pathological backtracking: Swift 5.7, NSRegularExpression 0.0001s vs Swift Regex 0.25s ('1000x'); Swift 6.1.2 on M3, 9.167 s for one match and 'It is 4x faster to use NSRegularExpression'. swift-format lint of swift-syntax: 47796699574 instructions (static Regex) vs 47465967198 (static NSRegularExpression), 0.7% (derived from page data); Regex rebuilt per file 49422947117.
workload: Construction loop of a comment-matching pattern; '^ +A' against 50,000 spaces; '.*\[' against a long run of 'a'; swift-format lint of the swift-syntax repository.
hardware: Intel iMac (2022 report); Apple M3 (2025 report)
toolchain: Swift 5.7 (2022); Apple Swift 6.1.2 (2025); release builds for swift-format
one_liner: Foundation's ICU regex is ~19x cheaper to construct than Swift Regex and avoids some backtracking cliffs; matching is near parity once cached.
how_it_is_fast: NSRegularExpression compiles patterns with ICU's mature C engine and matches over UTF-16. Swift Regex compiles to its own bytecode with grapheme-cluster semantics by default; on one large match benchmark its maintainers found more time going to retain/release, copy-on-write arrays and walking String's higher-level representation than to matching itself.
use_it_when: Patterns built from strings at runtime, especially when created repeatedly
Patterns that hit Swift Regex's known backtracking problems (issue 483, still open)
skip_it_when: Regexes created once and reused, where matching cost is close to parity
Code that needs typed captures, RegexBuilder or Unicode grapheme-correct matching
caveats: The 1000x figure is from Swift 5.7 (2022); the tracking issue is still open in 2026 but the case has not been re-measured publicly.

Swift Regex did get faster: 2023 changes cut some benchmarks by up to 57%, and maintainers measured a further ~1.5x in late 2024, but a forum user found Swift 6.3-dev 'quite the same' on a large match benchmark that remains ~10x slower than Java.
No public suite compares the two across typical patterns on current toolchains.
Instruction counts, not wall time, for the swift-format comparison.
tradeoffs: Stringly typed patterns and NSRange-based results.
UTF-16 semantics rather than Character semantics.

evidence.quote: Today I tried to use the new Regex from Swift 5.7 to parse CSS variables in a 2000 line CSS file.
The old NSRegularExpression class performed the job in 0.0001s on my Intel iMac whereas the new Regex takes 1000x longer, namely 0.25s.
From my tests on M3 CPU
Just tried 6.3-dev and it is quite the same as before.
still shows a 10x factor between Java and Swift
